title: Redwood Security & Compliance Review — Incident Response, BCDR, SLA
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez, Liam Chen (Redwood); Sasha Patel, Mark Reynolds, Tina Gomez (Beacon Health)
Links shared: Redwood SOC 2 attestation (link), SLA doc (link), IR runbook (link - redacted)

Summary:
Quick review of SOC 2/ISO posture then deep dive on incident response, BCDR, RTO/RPO targets, uptime SLAs and escalation paths. Customer asked about paging, runbooks, post-incident RCA timelines and evidence for audit. Redwood agreed to share updated runbook and schedule a tabletop exercise.

Topics: SOC2/ISO status; RBAC/SSO & audit logs; encryption/KMS; incident response (IR) workflow; BCDR RTO/RPO; uptime & SLA; escalation process & contact lists.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava: hey everyone thanks for joining, we are going to go through our security posture and specifically incident response and business continuity, so maybe quick intros?
[00:12] Sasha: Sasha Patel, CISO at Beacon Health, thanks. We run a hybrid multi-cloud and have strict RTOs for patient-facing services.
[00:20] Mark: Mark Reynolds, cloud infra. Interested in details around DR and recovery for any Redwood-hosted inference endpoints.
[00:26] Tina: Tina Gomez, compliance, i'll be focusing on auditability and evidence for our ISO and internal audits.
[00:32] Liam: Liam Chen, solutions engineer at Redwood, i'll take the technical deep dive.
[00:36] Ava: perfect. quick agenda — SOC2/ISO certs, auth and audit logs, encryption/KMS, then IR + BCDR and SLA / escalation.

[02:03] Sasha: quick question before we start, do you maintain SOC 2 type ii? the doc link you sent says "SOC two" in the filename, can you confirm time frame?
[02:20] Ava: yes, SOC 2 Type II current through Nov 2024, we also have ISO 27001 certificate in progress, the attestation is the link i shared. apologies if auto-exports say SOC two, transcription quirk.

[04:10] Mark: for RBAC and SSO — we need SAML 2.0 and SCIM for user provisioning. also want to know how audit logs are retained and whether they can be exported to our SIEM.
[04:30] Liam: we support SAML SSO and SCIM; RBAC is role-based at the org and project level. audit logs are stored in immutable append-only storage for 1 year by default, exports to your SIEM via push or S3 export, retention configurable for enterprise plans. tiny caveat, export uses signed S3 presigned urls, we can set up a direct push to your SIEM via webhook if that's preferred — slight transcription: "SAML" sometimes shows as "S-A-M-L" in the automated notes.

[06:05] Tina: does audit log include token-level request context (model, route, requestor)? for compliance we need evidence showing who invoked what and when.
[06:20] Liam: yes logs contain request metadata: route, model id/version, user id, token counters, latency and error codes. note: we do not log raw prompt contents for customer-managed private deployments unless explicitly enabled; hosted API has configurable PII scrubbing and retention windows.

[08:30] Sasha: encryption — at rest and in transit, KMS integration, customer-managed keys?
[08:45] Ava: in transit is TLS 1.2/1.3. at rest we encrypt with AES-256. for Dedicated/Private we support CMEK via major KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). centralized key rotation is supported, and we can provide evidence of key policies during audit.

[10:40] Mark: good. now incident response: what's your RTO/RPO targets for hosted vs dedicated? and how do you notify customers if we hit an incident impacting availability?
[10:55] Liam: for Hosted API our internal SLOs aim at 99.95% uptime across model endpoints; Dedicated offers SLA-backed tiers — e.g., 99.9% or 99.95% depending on contract. RTO for critical incidents is <1 hour for failover initiation, RPO depends on workload and KV/prefix caching — typical RPO targets are under 5 minutes for system config, but for stateful sessions we recommend explicit session checkpointing if you need sub-minute RPO.
[11:30] Sasha: can you clarify that — the RPO "under 5 minutes" for system config makes sense, but for inference workloads we need clarity on if cached KV entries will be lost during failover.
[11:45] Liam: yes cached KV is best-effort; our continuous KV replication is in development for cross-az redundancy. current design: KV caches live in-memory per instance, we persist checkpoints to a cache store every X seconds (configurable). on Dedicated we can configure a shared Redis/Aerospike replicate which gives tighter RPOs. we'll document recommended patterns in the runbook.

[14:00] Tina: escalation paths — who do we page, and what's the priority ladder? we need a named contact for P1 with phone and pagers for our on-call ops.
[14:18] Ava: we have a multi-tier escalation: first alert to Redwood SRE runbook which triggers paging to on-call engineer, then on-call lead, then engineering manager, then product + AE. For enterprise deals we provide a named escalation contact (phone + email) and can support a dedicated Slack channel and a PagerDuty integration.

[16:02] Mark: what about post-incident deliverables? for audits we need incident timeline, RCA, mitigations, and artifact evidence within 72 hours.
[16:20] Liam: our standard practice: initial incident notification within 15–30 minutes for P1; preliminary impact and mitigation plan within 2 hours; full RCA and post-mortem within 72 hours. artifacts: logs, packet captures if network, timeline, configuration diffs. for sensitive customers we can provide redacted artifacts suitable for sharing with auditors.

[18:50] Sasha: is there an escalation SLA? e.g., when do you escalate to execs?
[19:05] Ava: for incidents classified as P1 with <99.9% degradation affecting production, escalation to execs happens within 4 hours. exec updates cadence is agreed in the contract.

[21:40] Tina: continuity — BCDR, do you have cold/hot standby strategies? geographic failover?
[21:58] Liam: yes, we run cross-region clusters for Dedicated enterprise deployments; Hosted API uses multi-region active-passive for some models and active-active for core infra. Hot standby available for Dedicated with warm replicas; we support failover drills on request. RTO varies: active-active services have near-zero failover, active-passive is usually sub-1 hour for DNS and routing convergence plus instance spin-up.

[24:10] Mark: DNS TTLs and cache invalidation are a concern for us — what’s typical TTL during failover?
[24:25] Liam: we recommend low TTLs (~30s-60s) during planned failover windows; for emergency drills we coordinate with your infra to lower cache TTLs ahead of time. some CDNs and corporate proxies may still cache longer, we provide signed objectives to help.

[26:00] Sasha: tabletop exercises — can Redwood run one with our team? we want a mock P1 and a mock data-exfil scenario and see how runbooks perform.
[26:15] Ava: yes we can. we offer a SOC/IR tabletop run through that covers detection, triage, containment, eradication and lessons learned. typically 2–4 hours. we also can provide a customized runbook for Beacon.

[28:40] Tina: auditability again — timeline artifacts must be tamper-evident. do you provide signed logs or hash chains?
[28:55] Liam: logs are write-once with integrity checks. we provide cryptographic checksums for exported log bundles and can support HSM-backed signing for enterprise. note: terminology in auto-transcripts sometimes munges HSM to "H-S-M" — apologies.

[31:10] Mark: what about legal notifications and breach thresholds? do you have a contract clause for notification windows?
[31:25] Ava: yes breach notification windows are contract dependent but typically we notify customers within 72 hours of confirming an incident that meets breach criteria; for regulated data we can commit to tighter windows in the contract. we loop legal and security and supply customer-facing communications templates.

[33:05] Sasha: for SLA credits and uptime — how are credits calculated? also what are the excluded downtime windows?
[33:20] Liam: credits are calculated as a percentage of monthly fees prorated against downtime and per the SLA table. planned maintenance windows and customer misconfigurations are excluded. SLA doc includes examples and calculation formula — i’ll share link and a short explainer.

[35:40] Mark: monitoring and alerts — do you expose health endpoints and metrics so our SREs can set alerts on latency and error budgets?
[35:55] Liam: yes we expose metrics via Prometheus endpoint for Dedicated and private; Hosted we supply per-route metrics via the console and can push metrics to your monitoring via a metrics exporter. we also offer webhooks/AlertManager and PagerDuty integrations.

[38:10] Sasha: regulatory: data residency requirements — we need data to remain in EEA for a particular product line. how do you ensure region isolation?
[38:25] Ava: we support region-specific tenancy. Dedicated and Private allow you to pin to a region and we can restrict backups and logs to that region. for hosted accounts we offer EEA-only hosting tiers and contractual commitments on data residency.

[40:50] Tina: encryption key custody question: do you ever hold KEKs for customer-managed keys?
[41:05] Liam: we do not hold KEKs if you opt for CMEK; keys stay in your KMS. Redwood will have wrapped keys for ephemeral operations but master KEK control remains with you. for convenience we can support a split custody arrangement for certain enterprise deals.

[43:20] Mark: incident simulation — if we wanted to test a failover tomorrow — what's the minimum notice and what do you need from our side?
[43:35] Ava: for a coordinated failover drill we prefer 72 hours notice. we need a point of contact, desired RTO goals, affected endpoints, and preferred maintenance window. for unannounced drills we can do tabletop only.

[46:00] Sasha: can you walk through the escalation contacts and provide a single page we can put in our runbook?
[46:12] Liam: yes; i'll prepare a one-page escalation matrix: on-call phone, escalation ladder, PagerDuty integration id, exec contact. also include example incident classification (P0/P1/P2) and triggers.

[48:30] Tina: onboarding evidence — during our ISO recert, we may need signed SOC 2 report, configuration snapshots and proof of runbook execution. can you provide those artifacts?
[48:45] Ava: yes SOC 2 report, config snapshots, audit logs, and runbook change history are available. for some artifacts we require an NDA for extra-sensitivity docs, but normally we can provide redacted copies.

[50:10] Mark: any known limitations we should be aware of? you mentioned KV checkpointing is best-effort currently. anything else?
[50:25] Liam: two items: (1) in-memory KV not replicated cross-region by default, though Dedicated can be configured with shared caching; (2) cold-starts for large models can affect RTO; we recommend warm pools for critical endpoints. we'll include these mitigations in the runbook.

[52:00] Ava: wrapping up — recap of next steps.
[52:10] Sasha: go ahead.
[52:12] Ava: we'll share: 1) SOC2 attestation and ISO status; 2) detailed IR runbook and one-page escalation matrix; 3) SLA doc and credit calc example; 4) propose dates for a tabletop exercise; 5) config recommendations for KV persistence and CMEK setup.
[52:32] Tina: thanks, also please include sample RCA templates you use.
[52:38] Liam: will do.
[53:00] Ava: we'll follow up with a Collab email and attach the artifacts, propose two windows for the tabletop. any final Qs?
[53:10] Sasha: no, that's it, thanks all.
[53:17] Ava: thanks everyone.
summary: Redwood reviewed SOC 2/ISO posture, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, encryption/KMS and then did a detailed walkthrough of incident response (IR) and business continuity/disaster recovery (BCDR). Key outcomes: Redwood confirmed SOC2 Type II; described RBAC, SAML/SCIM support, and log retention/export options; described encryption and CMEK support; provided RTO/RPO targets and caveats about in-memory KV cache; described escalation ladder, PagerDuty/phone integration, and post-incident deliverables (initial notice, preliminary impact, and full RCA within 72 hours). Agreed next steps to share SOC2, runbook, SLA doc, and schedule a tabletop exercise.
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC 2 Type II report and current ISO status (link)
Redwood to provide detailed IR runbook and one-page escalation matrix
Redwood to send SLA doc + credit calculation example
Schedule tabletop exercise (Redwood to propose two windows)
Provide config recommendations for KV persistence and CMEK setup

Ava Martinez: circulate SOC2 attestation, SLA doc and IR runbook to Beacon; due 2025-02-14
Beacon (Sasha/Tina): confirm tabletop exercise participants and preferred windows; due 2025-02-18
